status_definitions.STATICALLY_RESOLVED: Enough static/deterministic evidence exists that no runtime observation is required for this bounded question.
status_definitions.STATICALLY_SOLVABLE: Not solved yet, but concrete static avenues remain (named files/functions/techniques); never placed in the runtime backlog.
status_definitions.STATICALLY_AMBIGUOUS: Extensive static work has narrowed the possibilities to two or more remaining interpretations; runtime may eventually be needed only after the relevant static graph is exhausted.
status_definitions.RUNTIME_ESSENTIAL: The answer fundamentally depends on dynamic information no static evidence can supply.

questions.question: Is the UI-script container format used by all .big screen packages (member types .apt/.const/.o/.msh) identified, and is there a proven mechanism connecting UI scripts to BOOT.BIN native functions?
questions.evidence: A THIRD resource/code-dispatch mechanism was found this delta pass, distinct from the bitmask dispatcher and the data-driven registry table above. Each of this pass's 11 newly-added .big files (10 BIGF-format, all uncompressed members) contains a .apt (compiled UI-script bytecode) and a paired .const member. The .const format was fully decoded: a fixed 20-byte signature 'Apt constant file\x1a\x00\x00', followed by 3 LE u32 fields (a size/pool field, an entry `count`, and a `header_len`=0x20), followed by `count` (tag=1,string_offset) pairs, followed by a flat NUL-terminated string pool holding every identifier/constant name the compiled .apt bytecode references (totals observed this pass: 890/862/17/126/534/10/144/126/113/397 names across the 10 files). Separately, EVERY 'GetXxxInfo'/'SetXxxInfo'/'DEBUG_GetXxxData'-style native-function name found this pass (GetSelectBoxerInfo, GetOptionsSettings, DEBUG_GetDebugMenuData, GetAdhocRivalsInfo/GetAdhocRivalsUserInfo, GetCareerHistoryInfo, GetRecordBooksInfo, etc.) is owned in BOOT.BIN by a small (~20-50 instruction) function that does nothing but call a SHARED pair of functions, func_0CDAC0/func_0CDA70, repeatedly, once per native name, each call passing (name_string_ptr, screen_class_string_ptr, -1). This is proven, by structure, to be a generic 'register native function under this name for this UI screen class' mechanism used identically by every one of the 11 files' native accessors -- these small functions are registration glue, not the data-producing implementations themselves.
questions.remaining_static_work: Trace how func_0CDAC0/func_0CDA70's registration is later resolved/dispatched at script-call time (i.e. where the registered name string is looked up and its real implementation function invoked) -- this single mechanism gates nearly every UI-side lead opened by this delta pass (GetSelectBoxerInfo's real implementation, GetRecordBooksInfo's real implementation, etc.), so resolving it once would advance several other STATICALLY_SOLVABLE questions at once. Decoding the .apt bytecode format itself (to recover literal numeric constants such as the difficulty enum's 'm_arrValues') is a separate, larger undertaking not attempted this pass.

questions.question: What does func_00186464's 8-bit-masked linked-list index actually select (boxer record vs. table-instance registration)?
questions.evidence: RESOLVED during Overhaul Alpha 1's targeted static RE (analysis/resources/overhaul-alpha1-evidence.json entry alpha1-03). func_0018654C (a caller of func_00186464 flagged since the first boxer-schema pass) was disassembled in full: it walks func_186464(0), func_186464(1), ... via the proven 8-bit index until null, calling an INDIRECT FUNCTION POINTER read from a per-node vtable-like sub-table for each node (the same {i16,funcptr} shape already proven for the generic resource-table loader), then appends its own caller-supplied object onto the list's end by writing the found node's +0x10 'next' field (node->0x10 = new_object; new_object->0xC = node -- the previously-missing list-insertion writer). This is a table-instance REGISTRY append/measure pattern over heterogeneous nodes each queried via its own function pointer -- not a homogeneous boxer-record array. Boxer records are proven (program-04-02) to be indexed via xdbboxr.adf's own header word0 through func_001AD268, a completely separate mechanism. The 'table-instance registration' interpretation is confirmed; the 'boxer record' interpretation is ruled out.

questions.question: Is there a fixed maximum roster/boxer-database record count?
questions.evidence: xdbboxr.adf's header word0=121 is proven to be consumed as a count by real code, but whether 121 is a hard compiled maximum (vs. simply 'however many rows this specific database currently has') was not established -- no bounds-check or fixed-size array declaration referencing 121 as a compile-time constant was located. This delta pass inspected selectboxer.big!selectBoxer.const (397 named constants) specifically for a UI-authored boxer-count cap: none was found -- no MAX_BOXER/MAX_ROSTER-style constant exists in this file (a full MAX_/NUM_ scan across all 10 newly-added .const pools found only MAX_WEIGHTCLASS/NUM_STATS in selectboxer.big and generic display-pagination constants MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS/MAX_NUM_GROUPS/MAX_NUM_COLUMNS elsewhere, none of which bound the boxer roster itself). This is a genuine negative result, not just an absence of a positive one: it rules out one of the four originally-listed interpretations ('a UI-authored maximum') as unsupported by this file, though it cannot rule out an executable-side or save-format-side cap. selectBoxer.const does confirm the UI receives an explicit 'iListLength'/'iEndList' pair alongside 'objBoxerIDs' and a distinct 'bHasCustom' flag, consistent with the boxer list being handed to the UI as a native-supplied, already-counted array rather than a UI-enumerated fixed-size table.
questions.remaining_static_work: Search for a literal immediate 121 (0x79) used as an array-size bound or allocation size elsewhere in BOOT.BIN, independent of the header value itself. Also: reach GetSelectBoxerInfo's real implementation (see the func_00186464 entry above for the same registration-mechanism blocker) to observe what count value it actually computes and hands to iListLength.

questions.question: Does fnhud.hud's format expose named field bindings for stamina, health, damage, stun, knockdowns, rounds, timers, scorecards, judges, or boxer slots (relevant to programs 05/07/08/10/11's in-fight HUD data)?
questions.evidence: fnhud.hud (33,528 bytes) is NOT a BIGF archive -- it has the custom binary header already noted in the prior pass's backlog (magic bytes 01 00 f4 f1), now partially decoded: a repeating sequence of what appear to be (size, type_id, offset) u32 triples immediately following the 16-byte magic/version prefix. This delta pass extracted its full ASCII string content (151 unique runs) and found it is NOT a text-field-binding format the way the .apt/.const UI packages are -- it consists of short, tagged component/geometry-piece identifiers (4-character codes such as RN01-RN15, RC01-RC21, RCH1-RCH5, CM01-CM17, CD01-CD10, MH01-MH17, OL01-OL12, OV01-OV08, PU01-PU15, CY01-CY03, plus rendering-primitive keywords POLY/fill/flre/blnk/load/LINE). These read as a component-indexed vector-HUD-geometry container (glyph/digit/icon pieces for on-screen HUD rendering), not a semantic field-binding table like the .apt/.const files. Per this project's explicit discipline, no field semantics are inferred from these 4-character labels alone (e.g. 'RN' plausibly maps to round-number digit glyphs and 'RC' to round-card pieces, but this is not asserted as proven) -- this corrects the assumption that fnhud.hud would directly expose gameplay field names the way selectboxer.big/optionsettings.big did.
questions.remaining_static_work: Fully decode fnhud.hud's header table structure (the repeating size/type/offset triples) to establish an authoritative component hierarchy, then determine whether any component ties back to a BOOT.BIN-owned numeric field (e.g. via a renderer-consumer function) rather than inferring meaning from the 4-character tags alone.

questions.question: Does a named AI difficulty or fighting-style enum/table exist?
questions.evidence: RESOLVED this delta pass for the difficulty half of the question (the fighting-style half is split out as a separate, still-open question below). The prior session's BOOT.BIN-only string search found zero matches because the enum's names live in a resource file, not BOOT.BIN's own string table -- exactly the methodological blind spot this project has flagged before. A raw byte-level (not extracted-string-table) search of optionsettings.big found, at file offset 0x8548-0x8563, three consecutive NUL-terminated localization-key strings inside optionSettings.const's own data region: '$O_Easy\x00$O_Medium\x00\x00\x00$O_Hard\x00', immediately preceded by the field name 'm_arrText' and immediately followed by 'm_arrValues' -- i.e. a UI toggle-widget definition whose text array is literally ['$O_Easy', '$O_Medium', '$O_Hard'] paired with a companion numeric-values array. This is bound to the 'cpToggleDifficulty' widget (labeled via the localization key '$M_Difficulty', also found in the same file at 0x84e0). This is direct, unambiguous, static evidence: the retail game exposes a named, exactly-3-level difficulty enum (Easy / Medium / Hard) through its options-menu UI script. static_ceiling.definition: Count-based projection = STATICALLY_RESOLVED + STATICALLY_SOLVABLE, i.e. every question with either evidence already in hand or a concrete named static avenue remaining. STATICALLY_AMBIGUOUS questions are excluded from the ceiling because they are not proven closeable by static work alone yet (their alternatives may or may not collapse to one answer statically).

runtime_floor.definition: The list of ONLY questions currently classified RUNTIME_ESSENTIAL -- i.e. genuinely believed to require dynamic observation because no static avenue remains. Per task policy this list must be kept as small as evidence honestly allows and must NEVER include a question that still has a named static avenue (those belong in STATICALLY_SOLVABLE/STATICALLY_AMBIGUOUS instead).
